html:
A Senegalese writer and filmmaker, a former Tirailleur and dock worker in Marseille, called the father of African cinema.

His novel God's Bits of Wood (1960) told the story of the 1947 strike on the Dakar to Niger railway. He turned to film to reach people who could not read, and his Black Girl (1966) was the first feature by a sub-Saharan African director to win world notice. Later films, often in Wolof, took on the new elite (Xala), colonial crimes (Camp de Thiaroye) and female genital cutting (Moolaade, 2004). With the festival FESPACO he helped build African film.
sum: A Senegalese writer and filmmaker, a former Tirailleur and dock worker in Marseille, called the father of African cinema.
